notes:
Fast-track consent business: three complete items (81, 82, 83) plus the tail of item 80, all conducted by the chair alone, with one intervention by the secretary. DOES NOT OPEN MID-UTTERANCE: the fragment's first line is the centred bold link 'Orden del Día Nº 1653', which is printed matter, not speech. I checked the raw sitting file: immediately before the fragment the chair's turn ends with '(Orden del Día Nº 1653)' and the note '-- El texto es el siguiente:' closes it, so no utterance is in progress across the boundary and opens_mid_utterance is false. This is the one judgement in my three stretches I would most want a second opinion on, since a reader who treats the inserted order-of-the-day as part of the preceding speech would answer true. THE EASY TRAP: each item has the chair speak TWICE in a row with only a vote note between -- 'En consideración en general.' then, after '-- La votación resulta afirmativa.', 'Queda aprobada...'. Rule 2 says a note does not start a new turn, but these are two separate turns anyway because each carries its own printed label; what rule 2 covers here is the unlabelled 'Si no se hace uso de la palabra, se va a votar.' paragraph, which I folded into the preceding 'En consideración' turn every time (three times) rather than counting it. Counting those would inflate the total from 11 to 14. TYPIST ERROR PRESERVED: the secretary prints as 'Sr. Secretario (Oyarzún) . -- ' with a space between the holder and the full stop, unlike every other label in the file; I left it exactly so. INSERTED DOCUMENTS: each 'Orden del Día Nº NNNN' is a centred bold hyperlink to proyectos2.senado.gov.ar standing in for the text of the order of the day, which the export did not inline. It has no speaker and I invented none. I filed these four under furniture rather than headings because they are document pointers rather than section titles, but they are centred and bold and a different reader could plausibly file them as headings -- worth deciding once, repo-wide. HEADINGS: the section number ('81') is a separate centred bold paragraph and the title is a separate

; I listed each as its own entry, in printed order, rather than joining them into '81 Aniversario...'. MARKUP: labels here split the holder out of the bold on BOTH sides -- 'Sr. Presidente (Gioja). -- ' -- so the terminator sits in a second bold run; in the three 'Corresponde considerar' labels the source line even breaks between the stop and the dash. All print as 'Sr. Presidente (Gioja). --'. The '-- El texto es el siguiente:' notes put the dash OUTSIDE the italics ('-- El texto es el siguiente:'), unlike the vote notes, where the dash is inside; a parser keying on italic-starts-with-dash will miss those three.
